item.title: Hawaii DHS offers replacement SNAP benefits for Molokai households ahead of outages
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: The Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services says Molokaʻi households receiving SNAP benefits may apply for replacements due to anticipated food spoilage.
item.content:encoded:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - The Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services (DHS) says Molokaʻi households receiving SNAP benefits may apply for replacements due to anticipated outages.

Hawaiian Electric has announced that planned outages will occur from Oct. 3 through Oct. 8 as crews replace existing copper lines with aluminum conductors along East Kamehameha V Highway between Onioni Drive and Puʻu O Hōkū Ranch.

These outages are required to safely complete ongoing grid‑hardening work on Molokaʻi.

To support households who may experience food spoilage during these outages, DHS received approval from the USDA Food and Nutrition Administration to authorize replacement SNAP benefits.

Under standard federal rules, households have 10 days to apply after the date of food loss. SNAP participants requesting replacement benefits must submit a signed statement including:

  • Name of the SNAP participant
  • Date of food loss
  • Estimated value of food lost
  • Brief description of what occurred
  • Participant contact information

A sample statement is available on the DHS website, but applicants may submit their own written statement. Statements may be submitted to any DHS processing center statewide and a participant signature is required.

For more information, visit humanservices.hawaii.gov or call the Statewide Public Assistance Information Line at 1‑855‑643‑1643.

media:content.media:description: The Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services (DHS) says Molokaʻi households receiving SNAP benefits may apply for replacements due to anticipated outages.

item.title: Wainiha residents ‘really afraid’ of future storm impacts after Lowell devours sandbar
item.dc:creator: Aalii Dukelow
item.description: The sandbar was a buffer for oceanfront residents from high surf.
item.content:encoded:
KAUAI (HawaiiNewsNow) - Residents on Kauaʻi’s North Shore fear damage from Hurricane Lowell could lead to more destruction in the future.

The storm’s strong surges swept away a sandbar in Wainiha Bay that shielded oceanfront homes from high surf.

“So relieved that we made it through (the hurricane) and then in the morning to come, we looked out here and our entire beach was gone,” said beachside resident Mahinanani Antonia.

Without the bar buffering the shorebreak, Antonia said she is worried winter swells will impact her home.

Antonia’s concerns come as she processes the loss of her stepfather, who died about a week after the storm.

“Our family’s been here forever,” Antonia said. “The waters are rushing out right here and it’s actually just raking all of my under foundation away.”

Antonia added her house is not the only structure at risk, saying, “You can see it’s eroding the road too, so this is imperative that we get help.”

Other area residents have joined Antonia’s call for help, echoing her concerns over the reshaped landscape.

“It’s so important for us to have that sandbar, because it, the ocean comes in, it will erode our road, and we’re going to be totally, totally stranded down this way. We might even have to go with boat, we don’t know,” said Nancy Mae Chandler, who lost her own home up the road to floodwater.

Antonia emphasized, “When I see this, and the erosion, and I see no beach, I am really afraid. Please help us.”

Kauaʻi County officials gave Hawaii News Now the following statement:

“The County Planning Department is in discussions with landowners in this area and the Department of Land and Natural Resources, Office of Coastal Conservation Lands (DLNR, OCCL) to determine possible mitigation approaches. In balancing the needs of any shoreline abutting property owner, we also need to ensure that the coastal environment and its natural processes are not compromised.”

media:content.media:description: Hurricane Lowell swept away a sandbar in Wainiha that served as a buffer during high surf. Now, coastal residents worry winter swells could damage their homes.

item.title: Volunteers paint rainbow on Kailua crosswalk after tragedy near Kaelepulu Elementary
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Robbins
item.description: Kailua students designed a rainbow crosswalk mural on Keolu Drive to honor Jenifer Van Lent, killed in 2023, and to slow drivers near Kaʻelepulu Elementary.
item.content:encoded:
KAILUA (HawaiiNewsNow) - After tragedy struck near a Kailua public school, a community-led project driven by students’ vision has finally become reality after years of work.

On Keolu Drive near Kaʻelepulu Elementary School in Kailua, a flower-adorned post now marks where Jenifer Van Lent — a Kailua mother, Tūtū and retired educator — was killed in a crosswalk in January 2023 during an early morning walk in the neighborhood.

“Mom, I wish you were here,” said Sabrina Cervantes, Lent’s daughter.

Cervantes and family, including Lent’s grandsons, bring flowers weekly in remembrance of Lent, who they call “Mama Jen.”

“We know you’re looking down on us from heaven, and we’ll look for you in the rainbows,” Cervantes said.

A rainbow has been painted in Mama Jen’s honor as part of a crosswalk mural designed by third- and fourth-graders at Kaʻelepulu.

The design was presented to the neighborhood board and received approval from the Honolulu mayor’s office. Some safety measures were taken in past years with “see me” flags, but cars continued speeding past the school and many parents feared letting students walk to school.

“We’re at the corner of Akiohala and Keolu Drive, just adjacent to Kaʻelepulu Elementary School,” said Kate Chang, parent and Kaʻelepulu Parents, Teachers and Students Association (PTSA) member. “We are here to install a street mural to help keep our community safe. It’s a collaboration and a partnership that started with concerned parents and the kids got involved designing a mural.”

Local artist Lauren Roth helped bring their vision to life, along with helping hands from the school’s PTSA.

“They learned the moʻolelo and they studied all the land and the stories of Kailua and they came up with this beautiful idea how to incorporate all those, stories into this artwork,” said Lauren Roth, a Kailua artist.

More than 70 volunteers came out to brighten Keolu Drive in hopes that cars would slow down.

Since it wasn’t safe on the road, students could not paint themselves, so adults took on the task to bring the students’ vision to life.

With one paint stroke at a time, the community is turning heartbreak into acts of aloha. Word got out that the school needed help, so volunteers showed up ready to help.

“We’re just painting, making sure all the kids’ dreams for what they came up with comes true, and, you know, try to bring out joy as much as possible,” said Elijah Odhiambo, who is stationed at Kaneohe Marine Corps base.

“A great way to bring the community together so this doesn’t happen again for anyone else’s family member; for the safety of everyone,” Cervantes said while painting part of the mural herself in memory of her mother.

“We picked bright colors that will hopefully have people slow down,” said Sara Wong, a Ka’elepulu teacher and student advisor. “The students created it so that it can be on the ground, keeping our community safe.”

There’s a safety purpose behind the color — visually narrowing the roadway and reminding drivers they are in a school zone.

“This is our mauka side, this is our ʻāina in the middle median, and then our makai side,” Chang said.

This week’s official blessing of the crosswalk paves the way for a positive tomorrow, thanks to the drawings and visions of these keiki.

“Hopefully, that will inspire other kids to do other great things, think big, and not ever feel limited,” Cervantes said.

Cervantes added she’s grateful for the students who helped make this a reality for her mom and to keep others in the community safe.

As volunteers gathered, a real rainbow appeared; a reminder that Mama Jen’s memory is still shining over this street. And a symbol of hope to keep others safe.

If your school is interested in designing a mural along a crosswalk to help maintain a safe route to school, email yamato.sasaki@honolulu.gov or call 808-768-8312.

media:content.media:description: Kailua students designed a rainbow crosswalk mural on Keolu Drive to honor Jenifer Van Lent, killed in 2023, and to slow drivers near Kaʻelepulu Elementary.

item.title: Puna man indicted on murder in fatal Hawaiian Paradise Park Community Center shooting
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: Hawaii County Prosecuting Attorney Kelden Waltjen announced a Hilo grand jury has indicted 49-year-old Bryant Guevarra of Puna.
item.content:encoded:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - Hawaii County Prosecuting Attorney Kelden Waltjen announced a Hilo grand jury has indicted 49-year-old Bryant Guevarra of Puna.

The indictment stems from a Sept. 19 shooting at the Hawaiian Paradise Park Community Center that killed 41-year-old Jose Manuel Adame Romero.

Following his arrest, Guevarra made his initial appearance in Hilo District Court on Sept. 22.

Guevarra appeared in Hilo Circuit Court Friday afternoon for his return on the indictment warrant. He was ordered to appear for a hearing on defense counsel’s motion for a bail reduction on Oct. 26.

His bail was maintained at $1.823 million. A jury trial is scheduled for Feb. 8, 2027.

Guevarra is charged with second-degree murder, carrying or use of a firearm in the commission of a separate felony, place to keep pistol or revolver, place to keep ammunition and reckless endangering in the first degree.

Second-degree murder carries a penalty of life in prison with the possibility of parole. Carrying or use of a firearm in the commission of a separate felony is a class A felony offense, which carries a penalty of a 20-year prison term.

The charges are allegations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

Initiated by Puna Patrol, the felony investigation was led by Detective Mike Matsumura from the Area I Criminal Investigation Section of the Hawai‘i Police Department. The case is being prosecuted by Deputy Prosecuting Attorneys Jeff Malate and Woodrow Pengelly.

Anyone having information to assist law enforcement should contact Crime Stoppers at (808) 961-8300.

media:content.media:description: Hawaii County Prosecuting Attorney Kelden Waltjen announced a Hilo grand jury has indicted 49-year-old Bryant Guevarra of Puna.

item.title: Hawaiian Electric assists National Park Service in restoring power to Kalaupapa
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: The restoration supports the return of residents following Hurricane Nolo.
item.content:encoded:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - Power has been restored to Kalaupapa after Hawaiian Electric assisted the National Park Service with repairs to a power line damaged by Hurricane Nolo along the Kalaupapa Pali.

The park service owns and maintains the electrical system serving Kalaupapa and coordinated repair efforts following an outage on Sept. 27.

Hurricane-force winds associated with Hurricane Nolo damaged the line serving the settlement. The primary issue was damage to the conductor extending from the top of the pali to the settlement below.

Hawaiian Electric provided personnel, equipment and helicopter support to help access and repair the damaged section of line in challenging terrain.

Restoring service required crews to access the remote ridge-top location and use helicopter support to install new conductor along the steep route down to Kalaupapa.

The restoration effort was delayed due to access issues from the property owner who controls the right of way at the top of the Kalaupapa Trail.

Approximately 60 Kalaupapa residents, patients and staff are one step closer to returning home after being temporarily relocated on Sept. 11.

Repairs to the settlement’s drinking water system and other repairs following impacts from Hurricane Nolo continue.

The restoration was made possible by the National Park Service, the Hawaiʻi Department of Health, Maui County and aviation partners.

media:content.media:description: Approximately 60 Kalaupapa residents, patients and staff are one step closer to returning home after being temporarily relocated on Sept. 11.

item.title: Fallen trooper among 3 officers killed in action from the same training class
item.dc:creator: Gilbert Corsey, Gray News staff
item.description: “It’s weird for sure; my first thought the other day was, ‘Man, is that class cursed,’” Brian Shirley said.
item.content:encoded:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. (WDRB+WAVE/Gray News) — A Kentucky father said he got chills when he learned Kentucky State Police Trooper Hayden Phillips was shot and killed Monday.

Phillips has a connection to two other officers killed in the line of duty. They all graduated from the same Department of Criminal Justice Training class at Eastern Kentucky University in December 2019.

“It’s weird for sure; my first thought the other day was, ‘Man, is that class cursed,’” Brian Shirley said.

Brian’s son, Jefferson County Sheriff’s Deputy Brandon Shirley, Kentucky State Police Trooper Hayden Phillips and Scott County Deputy Caleb Conley were among 33 graduates from DOJCT class 506.

All three were killed in action.

Brandon Shirley was ambushed in August 2021 while working private security in Louisville at a car lot off Rockford Lane. Conley was shot and killed while conducting a traffic stop on southbound Interstate 75 in Georgetown.

Conley’s murder is similar to what happened to Phillips, who died Monday in Warren County and was also shot during a traffic stop.

Shirley said the coincidence gave him chills.

“It definitely hits home every time I hear an officer has gone down,” he said.

He said when an officer dies, the loved ones left behind become part of a fraternity where no one wants membership, connected by grief.

“Heartache and sorrow, it’s just never going to shut off for them,” Shirley said. “My heart has a giant hole in it, and no matter what I pour into it, I’m never, ever going to fill it up.”

Shirley went to Conley’s funeral in 2023 and said he will connect with Phillips’ family as well.

“Those kids lost their dad,” Shirley said. “She lost her husband.”

They are new members in the club no one wants to join: law enforcement loved ones left behind.

“They say time heals all wounds,” Shirley said. “I don’t know if it gets better or you just get better at dealing with it.”

Police said Emonnie Branch, 51, of Portland, Tennessee, allegedly shot Phillips and fled, triggering a statewide manhunt.

Branch was later arrested in Louisville and charged with murder of a first responder in Phillips’ death. During his arraignment in Warren County Tuesday morning, a judge denied Branch bail.

According to court records from the Tennessee Department of Correction, Branch had at least one active warrant out for his arrest when Phillips stopped him. It was for a probation violation in a fraud case. He pleaded guilty to fraud and impersonation and was sentenced to five years’ probation in July of last year.

item.title: Bicyclist dies after being struck by vehicle near Keehi Marina
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: As a result, the bicyclist was ejected onto the roadway and was pronounced dead at the scene.
item.content:encoded:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - A bicyclist was killed Friday morning after being struck by a vehicle on Sand Island Access Road near Keehi Marina.

The incident happened at 7:10 a.m.

The Honolulu Police Department said a 34-year-old man was driving eastbound on Sand Island Access Road near Keehi Marina Boat Harbor when he struck a bicyclist, an unidentified man, who was traveling on Sand Island Access in the same direction.

As a result, the bicyclist was ejected onto the roadway and was pronounced dead at the scene. Police said the bicyclist was not wearing a helmet.

The 34-year-old driver and his 34-year-old passenger were not injured as a result of the collision.

At this time, speed, drugs, or alcohol do not appear to be a contributing factor in this collision.

This is the 31st traffic fatality on Oahu this year, compared to 68 at the same time in 2025.

The investigation is ongoing and no further information is available at this time.

media:content.media:description: The incident happened at 7:10 a.m.

item.title: Launch ramp at Port Allen Small Boat Harbor reopens
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: The launch ramp at Port Allen Small Boat Harbor in Hanapēpē Bay reopened Friday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
LĪHUʻE (HawaiiNewsNow) - The launch ramp at Port Allen Small Boat Harbor in Hanapēpē Bay reopened Friday afternoon.

The Department of Land and Natural Resources Division of Boating and Ocean Recreation completed both an engineering site inspection and a sonar survey of the harbor waters and seafloor.

According to DLNR officials, the launch ramp is safe for use and there are no navigational hazards to boating.

Harbor slips and moorings are still closed due to the extensive damage from Hurricane Lowell.

“We understand the importance of this facility to the people of Kauaʻi and are using all available resources to ensure that their access to the ocean from Port Allen will be restored as quickly as possible,” said Board of Land and Natural Resources Chairperson Ryan Kanakaʻole.

Anyone with questions about harbor and ramp access can contact the Port Allen Harbor Office at 808-335-8400.

media:content.media:description: The launch ramp at Port Allen Small Boat Harbor in Hanapēpē Bay reopened Friday afternoon.

item.title: Hawaii DOH warns of Sierra Nevada raw milk cheese recall over E. coli contamination
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: The Hawai‘i Department of Health’s Food and Drug Branch is alerting residents to a cheese recall over potential E. coli contamination.
item.content:encoded:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - The Hawai‘i Department of Health’s Food and Drug Branch is alerting residents to a cheese recall over potential E. coli contamination.

The voluntary recall by Sierra Nevada Cheese Company includes its Graziers Monterey Jack, Jalapeno Jack, Medium Cheddar and Sharp Cheddar raw milk cheeses.

The company initiated the recall after being contacted by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regarding the ongoing outbreak investigation.

The recalled products were distributed nationwide, including retailers like Down to Earth in Hawai‘i.

The FDB is working with the local stores to ensure that the recalled products are no longer available for sale.

To date, 13 illnesses have been associated with Graziers Raw Milk Medium Cheddar in a multistate outbreak of E. coli O26:H11.

There have been no reported cases of injury or illness in Hawai‘i to date.

E. coli strain symptoms

Escherichia coli O26:H11 is a strain type that produces the Shiga toxin, which can cause serious and sometimes fatal infections in young children, elderly people and others with weakened immune systems.

Symptoms of infection include severe stomach cramps, diarrhea, fever, nausea and/or vomiting. The strain type can cause acute diarrheal illness (often with bloody stools) within a few days of ingestion of the bacteria.

Most people recover within a week.

However, a subset of infected individuals – especially children under 5 years of age, the elderly and immunocompromised individuals – may develop Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), a severe illness causing red cell breakdown, low platelet count and renal failure.

HUS can lead to death.

Health advisories

The DOH advises affected individuals to contact a healthcare provider immediately if you are exhibiting symptoms after having consumed any of the recalled products.

The recalled products should no longer be available for purchase but may still be in consumers’ refrigerators or freezers.

Consumers who purchased the recalled products should not consume or serve them.

Return the products to the place of purchase for a refund or dispose of them in a sealed zip-top bag.

The FDB also recommends cleaning and sanitizing all surfaces that have come into contact with the products to reduce the risk of cross-contamination.

Consumers with questions can contact Sierra Nevada Cheese Company at 530-934-8662, Monday through Friday from 5:30 a.m. to 2 p.m. HST, or by email at recallinfo@sierranevadacheese.com.

media:content.media:description: The voluntary recall by Sierra Nevada Cheese Company includes its Graziers Monterey Jack, Jalapeno Jack, Medium Cheddar and Sharp Cheddar raw milk cheeses.

item.title: Firefighters extinguish 2-alarm fire at Leeward Drive Inn restaurant in Waipahu
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: Honolulu Fire Department crews were called out to the scene near Farrington Highway and Pupukahi Street just before 4:30 a.m. on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
WAIPAHU (HawaiiNewsNow) - Firefighters battled a 2-alarm building fire at Leeward Drive Inn, a landmark Korean restaurant in Waipahu early Friday morning.

Honolulu Fire Department crews were called out to the scene near Farrington Highway and Pupukahi Street just before 4:30 a.m. on Friday.

The first unit arrived at 4:35 a.m. and found smoke on all sides and flames through the roof.

Firefighters secured a water supply and initiated an aggressive offensive fire attack with an aerial ladder fire stream and handlines.

Overhaul techniques were performed on the rooftop and in the ceiling to extinguish smoldering materials while looking for hidden fires.

The fire was extinguished at 6:50 a.m., and the scene was cleared shortly after.

The restaurant will be closed Friday after the building sustained extensive interior damage.

No one was injured, and HFD said all searches confirmed no one was inside.

The HFD Fire Investigator was requested to determine the origin and cause of the fire and provide damage estimates.

Honolulu police and Emergency Medical Services were also on the scene.

media:content.media:description: The restaurant will be closed Friday after the building sustained extensive interior damage.

item.title: Maui man admits to selling meth and cocaine
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: A 37-year-old man known as “Dougie 2 Fresh” pleaded guilty Oct. 2 to two counts of distributing more than 50 grams of methamphetamine, U.S. Attorney Ken Sorenson announced.
item.content:encoded:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - A 37-year-old man known as “Dougie 2 Fresh” pleaded guilty Oct. 2 to two counts of distributing more than 50 grams of methamphetamine, U.S. Attorney Ken Sorenson announced.

According to court records, Douglas Taylor agreed to sell a confidential source meth and cocaine over the course of 10 controlled buys.

As part of his plea agreement, Taylor admitted to selling 398.46 grams of meth and 33.916 grams of cocaine, between Oct. 2024 and Aug. 2025.

Taylor faces at least 10 years and up to life in prison, a fine of up to $10,000,000 and a term of supervised release.

Sentencing is scheduled for Jan. 19 next year before U.S. District Judge Jill A. Otake. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jeannette Graviss is prosecuting the case.

The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Maui Police Department conducted investigations as a part of Project Safe Neighborhoods – a Department of Justice initiative in collaboration with local law enforcement, prosecutors and public safety partners to combat violent crime and safeguard communities.

media:content.media:description: A 37-year-old man known as “Dougie 2 Fresh” pleaded guilty Oct. 2 to two counts of distributing more than 50 grams of methamphetamine, U.S. Attorney Ken Sorenson announced.

item.title: More than 100 pet rats found living in parked cars, police say
item.dc:creator: FOX 12 Staff, Gray News staff
item.description: More than 100 pet rats were found in two parked cars in Eugene last month, according to the police department.
item.content:encoded:
EUGENE, Ore. (KPTV/Gray News) - More than 100 pet rats were found in two parked cars in Eugene last month, according to the police department.

At about 10:30 a.m. on Sept. 23, officers and animal welfare were called to help with two cars being towed. Police said one of the cars, a blue Saturn, was covered by tarp and, when removed, officers could see several rats inside.

According to police, there were rat feces throughout the car, along with chewed-up seat cushions, trash, no food, and very little water.

More rats were found in a nearby gold Suburban.

Police said the owner of the rats claimed to have rescued them. The owner tried to help capture the rats and get them out of the cars using yogurt, but the rats were hard to catch.

Fifty-two rats in eight cages were taken to Greenhill Humane Society. Three of the rats reportedly gave birth to 18 newborn rats after arriving.

The cars were taken to a towing yard with rats still inside. Police said animal welfare was going to continue to provide food and water for the rats until Greenhill had room to take more.

Police said the case remains open under a neglect investigation.

media:content.media:description: More than 100 pet rats were found in parked cars in Eugene last month.

item.title: Portland Trail Blazers fire new play-by-play broadcaster hours after hiring announced
item.dc:creator: KPTV News staff, Jordan Gartner
item.description: The Portland Trail Blazers have fired newly hired play-by-play broadcaster Braiden Bell.
item.content:encoded:
PORTLAND, Ore. (KPTV/Gray News) - The Portland Trail Blazers have fired newly hired play-by-play broadcaster Braiden Bell.

According to a statement from the team, Bell’s termination stemmed from social media posts that violated team and league policies about racist, sexist and harmful comments.

“The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist or harmful comments,” the team said with the announcement. “The play-by-play role carries a long legacy of excellence ... and we hold that standard without exception.”

Bell had been announced as the team’s new play-by-play announcer just hours before his firing.

“We did not meet our own bar in this process, and for that we apologize to Blazers fans and Rip City,” the team continued. “We will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects our values.”

Bell graduated from Arizona State University, where he called games for the basketball team.

Before his brief stint with the Trail Blazers, Bell also called games for California Baptist University, as well as being the play-by-play announcer for the Phoenix Mercury and working games in the NBA G League.

Bell said he was “deeply sorry” for the language that he used in previous posts on social media following his dismissal from the team.

“Those tweets, while wrong, were written by me 14 years ago while I was only 15 years old and have no reflection of who I am today. I do not take lightly any harm it causes now,” Bell’s message read. “I’d like to apologize to anyone who was hurt by my words and will continue to always treat people with kindness and respect.”

The 2026-27 NBA regular season begins on Oct. 20, with the Trail Blazers’ first preseason game scheduled for Oct. 7.

media:content.media:description: Bell, an Arizona State University graduate, served as the play-by-play announcer for Sun Devil Athletics and the Valley Suns in 2024 before joining the Mercury in 2025.

item.title: 911 call reveals concerns about well-being of 2 children found dead from starvation at home
item.dc:creator: Marissa Thompson, Elijah Brown, Jordan Gartner
item.description: Two children who were found dead in a home earlier this week in South Carolina have been identified.
item.content:encoded:
LADSON, S.C. (WCSC/Gray News) — Two children who were found dead in a home earlier this week in South Carolina have been identified, and authorities said this wasn’t the first time they had been called to the residence.

Emory Deacon, 2, and Harlow Deacon, 15 months old, died of starvation and dehydration due to neglect, Charleston County coroner Bobbi Jo O’Neal said.

Justine May, the children’s mother and described as their primary caregiver, has been charged in the case with two counts of homicide by child abuse.

According to the Charleston County Sheriff’s Office, deputies had responded to numerous calls at the Pinewood Drive residence before ultimately finding the two children dead during a welfare check at the home.

The previous calls to the home were said to have included welfare checks and visits coordinated with the South Carolina Department of Social Services and the South Carolina Department of Mental Health Mobile Crisis Unit.

Authorities said deputies made contact with May and the children in August and again several more times in September, noting they observed no signs of concern during those visits.

On Tuesday, authorities said they were called back to the home after a 911 call came through that morning asking deputies to conduct a welfare check on the two young girls after they had not been seen, with their mother acting differently while walking around the neighborhood by herself.

“I’m just concerned because she didn’t have her kids, and nobody has seen her kids,” the caller told the Charleston County 911 dispatcher. “She was walking down the road today, and she didn’t have her babies, and that’s not like her.”

When deputies arrived at the home that afternoon, they said May exited the house and was crying and speaking incoherently. Upon entering, that’s when they saw the two children dead.

May was taken into custody.

According to affidavits, after being read her Miranda rights, May told detectives that she had spent the previous two weeks in a “blur,” saying she could not remember the last time she fed Emory and Harlow or gave them anything to drink.

Authorities said May told detectives that she believed her children were dead because they did not eat. She reportedly told deputies that she knew that not feeding her children was neglectful and confirmed she had been the only one present at home and was the sole caregiver for the girls over the last few weeks.

May remains jailed at the Al Cannon Detention Center.

media:content.media:description: Hawlow Deason (left), Justine May (middle), Emory Deason.

item.title: Recycling facility helps police catch suspect after 77 fire hydrants damaged
item.dc:creator: Casey Zanowic, Gray News staff
item.description: Scrap yards are usually full of metal and hidden treasures, but this week, one of those yards helped police haul in something else - a scrap thief.
item.content:encoded:
ST. LOUIS (KMOV/Gray News) - Scrap yards are usually full of metal and hidden treasures, but this week, one of those yards helped police haul in something else - a scrap thief.

“Naturally, when they approached me, I was very happy to help and do anything I could and step forward and give them the information they needed,” Phillip Harbison, general manager at SA Recycling in St. Louis, exclaimed.

The recycling facility, located off of the Broadway, helped find the man who put countless lives in jeopardy.

“I genuinely just dislike thieves; I’m not a fan of thieves at all,” Harbison stated. “So it’s very important to me to get them off the street, and especially when they’re doing things that can harm our community.”

Over the past week, police have been searching for a suspect accused of damaging and stealing the components off of 77 fire hydrants across the City of St. Louis.

On Thursday, police arrested 65-year-old Harry Farmer in connection with that vandalism after they said surveillance video caught him sawing off the hydrants’ brass valves.

“We had a citizen who came forward. We were able to get video of this individual. We were able to obtain a name, but we had to do a case to make sure that we got it right, got the evidence, and then we had to track down video at each one of these known locations,” Chief Robert Tracy, St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, said.

Farmer allegedly went to SA Recycling to sell the valves, which is when Harbison got him on camera and a picture of his ID.

“All the way from the second they pull onto this lot, they’re on camera,” he explained. “We have pictures of their ID; everything is stored in our database, so every transaction will have a picture of the material they brought in, of their ID, license plate, all of that.”

When police came to ask if they had any information about these incidents, Harbison said they were happy to cooperate.

“You don’t want those types of people out in the city and I want to stop the bad name that’s being given to scrap yards, and that’s why we keep the records we do and are able to help when the police do come and ask for help,” he stated.

Farmer has now been charged with eight felonies.

“Damaging fire hydrants creates a major public safety risk,” Chief Tracy said. “Firefighters depend on working hydrants to protect lives and property - interfering with that access puts residents, businesses and first responders in danger.”

“I’ve been Fire Chief for 19 years, been in this city for 48 with the fire department. I’ve never, ever seen anything like this. Traveled around the country, I’ve never seen hydrants vandalized like this intentionally,” Chief Dennis Jenkerson, St. Louis Fire Department, stated.

For recycling facilities like Harbisons, they just have one message to other scrap thieves.

“I will not buy it; don’t bring it to SA Recycling. SA Recycling does not want stolen scrap… some of us will absolutely do our part and help the community and put criminals behind bars," he said.

As of Friday evening, Farmer is in custody, but police still have to extradite him back to Missouri from Illinois.

The investigation remains ongoing. Police want anyone with more information on the damaged hydrants to contact 314-444-2500 and talk to District 4 detectives.

item.title: Grand jury indicts 24-year-old woman in fatal Kailua Target shooting
item.dc:creator: HNN Staff
item.description: The charges stem from a Sept. 26 shooting in the parking lot of the Target store in Kailua.
item.content:encoded:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - A grand jury indicted Hilinaikailimakualopali Keeno, 24, for murder in the second degree in connection with the fatal shooting of 30-year-old Thomas Malone.

Keeno was also indicted on charges of carrying or using a firearm in the commission of a separate felony and a place to keep. Prosecutors also charged her as a multiple offender.

The charges stem from a Sept. 26 shooting in the parking lot of the Target store in Kailua.

Murder in the second degree carries a maximum sentence of life imprisonment with the possibility of parole.

If a jury finds that the prosecution has met its burden for the imposition of extended terms of imprisonment, Keeno could face life imprisonment without the possibility of parole for murder in the second degree, life imprisonment for the class A felony, and up to 10 years for the class C felony.

Keeno is being held at the Oahu Community Corrections Center.

Keeno is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

item.title: Wife hid husband’s remains in freezer for up to 7 years to collect benefits, police say
item.dc:creator: Hannah Lee, Akim Powell
item.description: A woman in Alaska hid her late husband’s remains in a freezer for years in order to collect benefits, according to authorities.
item.content:encoded:
ANCHORAGE, Alaska. (KTUU/Gray News) - A woman in Alaska hid her late husband’s remains in a freezer for years in order to collect benefits, according to authorities.

Juneau police found the remains of Ross Pasquan inside a chest freezer on July 19. Police said he would have been 74 years old at the time of the discovery of his remains.

A family member had been cleaning out the property following the death of Pasquan’s wife, Sheryl Ann McDonald-Pasquan, who died on July 14, 2025, from natural causes.

Inside a storage shed, a family member discovered a locked freezer.

Police said the person found the key, opened the freezer and found a tarp-wrapped object that appeared to contain human remains. They closed the freezer and went directly to Juneau police.

The State Medical Examiner’s Office determined that Pasquan died of natural causes related to severe cardiovascular disease. Investigators believe Pasquan’s remains were placed in the freezer sometime between 2018 and 2025.

The investigation found that McDonald-Pasquan concealed his death and continued applying for and receiving benefits in his name until her death. Those benefits included Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend checks, Social Security benefits and retirement benefits.

Investigators also learned that a retirement benefit provider had not been notified of his death and was still depositing monthly payments into Pasquan’s account up until July 2026.

Investigators found no evidence that another person caused Pasquan’s death or helped McDonald-Pasquan in concealing his remains or collecting his benefits.

Witness interviews indicated that Pasquan had a history of significant health problems and that McDonald-Pasquan served as his primary caregiver. Witnesses said she explained his absence by telling them he had been moved to a care facility outside Juneau.

The investigation is now closed due to McDonald-Pasquan’s death.

item.title: Group of Seven to release barrels of stockpiled fuel
item.dc:creator: Caitrin Assaf
item.description: Amid record global diesel prices, a group of some of the world’s largest economies will release millions of barrels of stockpiled fuel in an effort to cap the soaring cost.
item.content:encoded:
WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The Group of Seven - a collection of some of the world’s largest economies - announced on Friday the release of 100 million barrels of fuel from its emergency stockpile following record-high fuel prices in September.

Oil prices have risen to record levels globally. The G7’s release of crude and diesel barrels marks a rare move intended to cap the cost of diesel.

The barrels come from the G7’s emergency stockpile, which is set aside for global supply shortages.

Wars in Ukraine and Iran have reduced the global fuel supply. Diesel has been particularly affected, with American farmers and the shipping industry facing a heavy impact.

With the midterm elections now days away, the Trump administration had considered restricting U.S. diesel exports, including a possible outright ban, to lower costs before November.

The G7’s release appears to end that possibility; the group’s statement said the release comes with an agreement among member nations not to limit energy exports to allied countries.

President Trump said in a Truth Social post the process will begin “immediately.” French President Emmanuel Macron said the release would happen over four months.

The move could reduce diesel prices by a few cents per gallon, according to experts, who added the effect would likely be temporary. Releasing stockpiled barrels does little to increase refinery capacity or production, experts said.

item.title: Catering business shut down after football team suffers food poisoning before game
item.dc:creator: Jayla Louis, Jordan Gartner
item.description: An unlicensed home-based catering business in Illinois has been ordered to cease operations after dozens of people were sickened.
item.content:encoded:
ROCK ISLAND, Ill. (KWQC/Gray News) - An unlicensed home-based catering business in Illinois has been ordered to cease operations after dozens of people were sickened at a football team dinner.

According to the Rock Island Health Department, it was notified of a foodborne illness outbreak that stemmed from a Rock Island football team dinner that took place on Sept. 24 in the school cafeteria.

Health department officials said the dinner was catered by a home-based business called Sunshine and Spice.

Players, coaches and parents who attended the dinner were served fajita chicken, seasoned taco beef, cheese, flour taco shells, cheesy pepper beans, cilantro corn rice and Pico de Gallo salsa.

Seventy-five people were served the meal, and at least 45 were reported sick, causing the team to postpone its homecoming football game.

Just hours after the dinner, 23 players, five coaches and three parents reported symptoms, which included vomiting and diarrhea.

Officials said no one was hospitalized, but one player did have to visit a doctor.

The health department reported that most symptoms were over within 24 hours.

Health department officials noted that they met with the owner of Sunshine and Spice and learned the business was unlicensed and not food-safety certified. They then ordered the business to shut down, with the option of getting properly certified.

Officials said the owner told the health department that all ingredients were purchased from the Moline Walmart, Spotted Apron in Geneseo and farmers’ markets in Davenport and Coal Valley.

Joshua Harris, owner of Sunshine and Spice, released the following statement regarding the situation:

“First, Sunshine and Spice wants to sincerely apologize and send even more prayers to anyone affected by last week’s Rock Island football team meal.

We provided a taco bar-style potluck before the team was dismissed to prepare for their homecoming game. All of the food purchased from Walmart was fully cooked. We put all of the leftovers in plastic bags provided by the team parents for anyone to take home.

We have cooked for numerous parents of the team/school in the past and have no reason ever to provide a sub-standard meal or purposely attempt any tampering shenanigans. We are saddened by this whole situation.

We have been working side by side with the Rock Island County Health Department and Rock Island City/County Law Enforcement Agencies to be a part of their continuing investigations.

Again, we want to extend our deepest apologies and continued prayers to those affected.”

The investigation into the food poisoning remained active pending test results for pathogens in the food seized by the county, health officials said.

item.title: ‘A psychopath’: Professional boxer arrested after 2-year-old dies, 1-year-old hurt in alleged abuse
item.dc:creator: David Baker, Micaela Marshall, Jordan Gartner
item.description: A professional boxer is facing a first-degree murder charge after police say he beat and killed his girlfriend’s 2-year-old son and abused his own 1-year-old child.
item.content:encoded:
MESA, Ariz. (KPHO/Gray News) — A professional boxer is facing a first-degree murder charge after police say he beat and killed his girlfriend’s 2-year-old son and abused his own 1-year-old child.

Mesa police said the situation started Tuesday when paramedics responded to an apartment for a child in medical distress. First responders rushed the toddler to a hospital, where he died from his injuries.

Doctors noted suspicious bruising was found across the child’s body and contacted police, triggering a homicide investigation.

Investigators identified Kishawn Porter, 23, a professional fighter, as the suspect in the case.

Authorities said that while Porter is a professional fighter, bruising found across his knuckles did not come from training or competition, but rather from fatal child abuse.

Porter was taken into police custody on Tuesday.

“Mr. Porter hit and punched the 2-year-old victim multiple times with either his hands and/or a sandal,” a prosecutor with the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office said during Porter’s initial court appearance.

During Porter’s court appearance, prosecutors outlined a violent juvenile history, telling the judge Porter has prior adjudications for child molestation and aggravated assault involving a restrained victim.

An autopsy conducted Wednesday by the Maricopa County medical examiner revealed catastrophic internal trauma on the child that included healing and acute rib fractures, a lacerated liver and a lacerated stomach, with blood found pooling in the abdomen.

“It takes a substantial amount of force to lacerate the stomach, and the injuries were all consistent with child abuse,” court records stated. “Based on the injuries, no one could have survived the severity.”

Forensic experts noted that the child’s healing rib fractures pointed to a pattern of ongoing violence in the home rather than an isolated incident.

“That means this wasn’t the only attack,” Dr. Roy Lubit, a forensic psychiatrist who specializes in child abuse cases, said. “The idea of beating and killing an infant indicates an almost basic lack of humanity. An individual who would do the acts that are alleged would almost be overwhelmingly likely to be a psychopath.”

Detectives said Porter also abused his own 1-year-old child by spanking him, hitting him in the mouth and slapping his torso and rib cage.

Formal charges regarding the allegations involving the 1-year-old have not yet been submitted to prosecutors.

Following his arrest, two combat sports promotions announced they had cut ties with Porter due to the severity of the charges.

A judge set Porter’s bond at $1.5 million.

media:content.media:description: Kishawn Porter, 23, was arrested Tuesday.
